body: claimed: M5 session (Claude) · 2026-11-10T03:35Z · worktree/branch issue/658-egui-037 · plan: bump egui, egui-winit and egui-wgpu to 0.37 (and wgpu to match), fix the API breaks in place, then run the ui suites, the structural tests and clippy.

**Blocked upstream: `egui_dock` has no egui 0.37 release yet.** Nothing was pushed.

- CamCraft's dock layout (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs`, `layout/mod.rs`) uses `egui_dock =0.21.1`, its newest release. That release depends on `egui ^0.36`, so bumping egui alone would put two eguis in the build.
- egui 0.37.0 and egui_kittest 0.37.0 are out (2026-10-15). egui_dock's 0.37 support is an **open, unmerged PR, Adanos020/egui_dock#354** ("Bump egui version to 0.37, fix deprecations", 2026-10-25).

**Decision:** wait for egui_dock's 0.37 release, then bump all four (`egui`, `egui-winit`, `egui-wgpu`, `egui_kittest` to =0.37.x, `egui_dock` to its matching release) in one PR.
- **Dropped: a git pin to that PR's branch.** It's unreleased and unreviewed code in the UI's core layout, and AGENTS.md wants a new or unusual dependency source decided by the maintainer.
- **Dropped: replacing `egui_dock`.** That's a far bigger change than this issue.

**Next step:** recheck when egui_dock publishes 0.22 (or whatever version targets egui 0.37). This blocks #659 and #655.

unclaim

**On hold (contributor, 2026-11-09):** no agent works the SolidCraft UI changes (#655 and its sub-issues #658, #659, #661) until the maintainer has reviewed and signed off on the direction. Please don't pick or claim this until then. The maintainer may mark it `P?` (paused).

## Estimate and proposed breakdown (agent, for the maintainer, 2026-11-12)

**Verdict:** `effort:high`; one throwaway trial, then 2-3 PRs. Still blocked on `egui_dock`, unless the maintainer accepts a bridge (options below). This is a read-only estimate: nothing was built, filed, labelled or claimed.

### Upstream, checked today
- **egui stack:** egui, egui-winit, egui-wgpu, eframe and egui_kittest are at 0.37.0 (2026-10-15, crates.io). There is no 0.37.1.
- **egui_dock:** newest is still 0.21.1 (2026-08-06), on `egui ^0.36`. The 0.37 pull request (egui_dock PR 354, opened 2026-10-25) is still open: no review, no comment, mergeable. It changes 16 lines, 6 of them in `src/` (`Id::new` to `Id::unique`, `ui.id()` to `ui.scope_id()`). Upstream `main` last moved on 2026-09-23. A `release-0.22` branch exists, but it is on egui 0.36. Nobody has named a release date.
- **wgpu and winit do not move:** egui-wgpu 0.37.0 still asks for `wgpu ^30.0` and `winit ^0.30.13`, which is our lock (30.0.1 / 0.30.13). Its changelog has one entry, a surface-config fix.
- **Rust:** egui 0.37 needs Rust 1.95. Our workspace says `rust-version = "1.90"`.
- **SolidCraft does not use egui_dock** (no `egui_dock` or `egui_tiles` in its `Cargo.lock`); its kit brings its own panels. If #655 goes ahead, our dock is replaced later, so whatever is done for egui_dock here is a bridge.

### What the work is
1. **Root `Cargo.toml`:** five pins to `=0.37.0`; the egui_dock source; `features = ["default_fonts"]` on `egui` (0.37 dropped it from the defaults, and without it there is no built-in font and kittest panics on a missing glyph); `rust-version` 1.90 to 1.95. The lock moves accesskit 0.24 to 0.25 and kittest 0.4 to 0.5.
2. **API changes that hit our code** (counted in `crates/ui`, non-test):
   - `Id::new` is deprecated: 13 sites in 12 files.
   - `Ui::id` is renamed `scope_id`: 12 sites in 8 files.
   - `WidgetType` is replaced by `Role`: 4 sites in `debug_info.rs`, `recent_drop.rs`, `window_chrome.rs`.
   - `Panel` constructors take `AsIdSalt`: 2 sites in `shell.rs`.
   - Not hit (0 sites): `ViewportCommand::Screenshot`, `AsId`, `global_theme_preference_switch`, `Clipboard::new`.

   That is about 30 mechanical lines in about 20 files.
3. **Renderer: low risk.** Our egui-wgpu surface is small: `Renderer::new`, `register_native_texture`, `update_egui_texture_from_wgpu_texture`, `update_buffers`, `render`, `update_texture`, `free_texture` and `ScreenDescriptor`, in `shell_window.rs`, `shell_window/frame.rs` and `shell_web.rs`. The 0.37 changelog touches none of them, and the 211 `wgpu::` sites in `viewport.rs` stay on wgpu 30.
4. **wasm:** eframe 0.37 wants `wasm-bindgen ^0.2.126` and `web-sys ^0.3.103`; our lock has 0.2.129 and 0.3.106, so `web/build-app-wasm.sh` needs no new CLI. One build confirms it.

### The real unknown is the tests
- egui_kittest 0.37 **fails a test when an input widget has no accessible name**. We have 58 input-widget sites (28 `ComboBox`, 15 `TextEdit`, 14 `DragValue`, 1 `Slider`) and 6 explicit labelling calls. Whether `prop_row` (245 uses) gives its control a name in egui's eyes cannot be told by reading.
- 0.37 rebuilt the accessibility tree for popups, menus, modals and panels, and hides invisible widgets. Our tests hold 111 role or AccessKit lines and 185 `Harness` uses in 40 files; the crate has 665 tests.
- "Roomier buttons and a larger corner radius" are mostly overridden by our tokens.
- The 3 PNG goldens (`egui_app.png`, `egui_app_light.png`, `egui_tool_editor.png`) will differ. They are release-lane and are not refreshed in the PR.

So the source edits are a known 30 lines; the test edits are a **guess of 50-300 lines**.

**What would firm it up:** one throwaway trial bump on a scratch branch, with egui_dock taken from the pull request's head commit for the trial only. It gives the exact compile errors, the number of red tests by cause, and whether the wasm build links. An hour or two of work; nothing merges.

### egui_dock: four ways (the maintainer's choice; B and C are `needs-maintainer`)
- **A. Wait for the release.** Free, no date.
- **B. Pin egui_dock by git `rev` to the pull request's head commit** until a release exists. It is 16 lines that can be read in full. Recommended if the bump is wanted before upstream moves.
- **C. Vendor egui_dock 0.21.1** (85 KB, MIT) with those 6 lines changed. No outside branch to depend on, but third-party code in our tree.
- **D. Replace egui_dock with our own layout.** Dropped again: the biggest of the four, and #655 would redo it.

**The urgency has changed.** This issue exists so we can pin SolidCraft's UI crates. Since 2026-11-10 those crates need SolidCraft's written permission (see the estimate on #655). Until that is settled, option A costs nothing.

### Risks
- **Tests:** the fallout above, across 665 tests.
- **Three shells:** native (our winit loop), web (eframe) and headless must all be re-checked; `gpu_select` and `gpu_init` on macOS Metal need a Mac.
- **Gate cost:** a root `Cargo.toml` change makes the quick tier fall back to batch.
- **Actions budget:** none; no trigger changes.

### Proposed sub-issues, in build order

| # | Title | Done means | Effort | Areas | Depends on | Start |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Research: trial bump to egui 0.37 on a scratch branch | a comment here with the compile errors, red tests by cause, and the wasm result; branch deleted | `effort:medium` | `area:build`, `area:ui` | - | today |
| 2 | UI: every input widget has an accessible name | each `ComboBox`, `TextEdit`, `DragValue` and `Slider` in `crates/ui` carries a name; a structural test walks the pages and fails on an unnamed input; green on 0.36.2 | `effort:medium` | `area:ui`, `accessibility` | - | today |
| 3 | Build: egui stack to 0.37 | the pins, `default_fonts`, Rust 1.95 and the API renames land; ui suites, structural tests and clippy green; the wasm page builds; no PNG changes | `effort:high` | `area:build`, `area:ui` | 1, 2, the egui_dock choice | waits on that choice (or on upstream) |
| 4 | Build: egui_dock back to its crates.io release | the git pin or vendored copy is gone; ui suites green | `effort:low` | `area:build` | 3, upstream release | waits on upstream (only after B or C) |

**Why `effort:high` and not medium:** the change is workspace-wide, touches three shells and exposes the whole UI test surface to new kittest rules. If the trial (row 1) shows fewer than about 20 red tests, row 3 is honest `effort:medium`.

**Labels:** this issue carries both `P2` and `P?`. AGENTS.md says `P?` stands instead of a priority, so one of them is for the maintainer to remove.

Maintainer (question dialog, 2026-11-12): this stays paused until SolidCraft answers the permission request (see #655). Filed from the breakdown above because they are useful either way: #1118 (trial bump on a scratch branch) and #1119 (accessible name on every input widget).

Waits on the permission request to SolidCraft: https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft/issues/15340 (posted 2026-11-12, tracked on #655). The egui bump itself is ours either way; pinning any SolidCraft crate after it is not.
